caption: One bootstrap script installs drivers AND joins the Kubernetes cluster -- in the same terraform apply.

eyebrow: Label, taint, then the device plugin
code:
kubectl label nodes gpu-worker-0 ... gpu-worker-5 \
  accelerator=nvidia-a100

kubectl taint nodes gpu-worker-0 ... gpu-worker-5 \
  nvidia.com/gpu=present:NoSchedule

kubectl apply -f nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset.yaml

kubectl describe node gpu-worker-0 | grep -A3 Capacity:
caption: Label pulls GPU pods in; taint keeps everything else out. Capacity should show nvidia.com/gpu: 1.

eyebrow: The proof: a real training Job
code:
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: defect-model-training-run-42
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      nodeSelector:
        accelerator: nvidia-a100
      tolerations:
        - key: nvidia.com/gpu
          operator: Exists
          effect: NoSchedule
      containers:
        - name: trainer
          resources:
            limits:
              nvidia.com/gpu: 4
      restartPolicy: Never
caption: Reaching Running state is the real proof -- quota, Terraform, drivers, and scheduling all lined up.
